title: 1. The arc of sympathy: from the cosmos to the brain, and what the texts do to that story
md:
**The hypothesis.** Sympathy was first a cosmic bond (Stoic *sympatheia*), then an occult quality of things, then a medical controversy (the weapon-salve), then a moral feeling (Hume, Smith), then a psychological capacity (*Einfühlung*, "empathy" in 1909). Separately, resonance became a physical mechanism and then a social theory (Rosa).

**The verdict, in short.** The sequence is real as a list of when each *new* sense first appears. It is wrong as a story of one sense replacing the last.
- The body is there from the start, not at the end.
- The occult quality was absorbed into mechanism, not expelled.
- The moral sympathy of the eighteenth century is a new concept that took the old word.
- In physics, "resonance" replaces "sympathy" only in the 1870s–90s, two centuries after the mechanism was found.
- *Ganying* 感應 does not pass through these stages at all.

**How to read the ids.** Ids without a prefix are in this concept. `harmony-kb:`, `magic-kb:` and `aliveness-kb:` ids are claims already held by those concepts; they are cited here, not copied. Partial (◐) claims are hedged in the text.

## Where sympathy was located, period by period

| Period | Main site | Other sites already present | Key claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before the Stoics | the body (bodily contagion between people) | | [[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-problemata-vii-things-from-sympathy), [[31]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#anc-crit-brouwer-sympathy-began-body-soul) ◐ |
| Stoic (3rd c. BCE – 2nd c. CE) | the cosmos, one body held by one *pneuma* | the body; signs and divination | [[2]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-chrysippus-krasis-pneuma-whole-sympathetic-with-itself), [[3]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-sextus-cosmos-unified-body-finger-cut), [[4]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/ancient#anc-cleomedes-sympathy-needs-one-pneuma) |
| Galen (2nd c. CE) | the body: organ suffering with organ | | [[32]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medical-ancient#anc-galen-sympathy-without-transport-spine), [[33]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medical-ancient#anc-galen-frenzy-brain-by-sympathy-not-idiopathy) |
| Neoplatonic (3rd–5th c.) | the cosmos as one *living being* with one soul | things (stones, plants), the rite | [[34]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neoplatonic#anc-plotinus-iv4-32-sympathy-by-likeness-at-distance), [[5]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-plotinus-magic-by-sympathy), [[6]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-proclus-sympathy-sacred-science) |
| Han China (3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE) | everything at once: omens, rulers, music, rain, the sick body | | [[35]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-ganying-spans-levels), [[36]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-cfl-body-answers-weather) |
| Song Neo-Confucian (11th–12th c.) | the pattern of all change, including the response of opposites | | [[37]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-chenghao-only-ganying), [[38]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-zhuxi-ganying-pattern-of-all-change) |
| Medieval and Renaissance | things: hidden powers, the wolf and the sheep | the cosmos (Porta's chain), the body (Fracastoro's *consensus* of members) | [[7]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/music#mus-barocci50-wolf-string-drum), [[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-sympathy-ladder), [[9]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#nm-porta-chain-cord-touched-trembles-consent-dissent), [[39]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/natural-magic#em-fracastoro-sympathy-hidden-agreement) |
| 1610s–1660s | a contested cure at a distance | the cosmos (the world soul), the body (the blood on the weapon) | [[10]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-goclenius-question), [[40]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medicine#em-helmont-dispute-natural-or-satanic), [[11]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-foster-no-sympathy), [[41]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-digby-atoms-carried-by-light) |
| 1660s–1760s | the body's nerves; between bodies it becomes a word for a mechanism | | [[42]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-boyle-amity-enmity-only-in-minds), [[12]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-whytt-1765-sentient-sympathetic-power) |
| 1726–1840 | the feelings: a moral sentiment | the body (Rousseau), the will (Schopenhauer) | [[43]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-butler-1726-so-much-one-body), [[44]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1739-sympathy-communication), [[45]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-changing-places-in-fancy), [[46]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-rousseau-1755-pitie-precedes-reflection) |
| 1873–1917 | aesthetic projection into forms, then knowledge of other minds | | [[47]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/aesthetics#feel-vischer-1873-objective-einfuehlung), [[48]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#emp-lipps-1903-einfuehlung-third-knowledge), [[49]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#feel-titchener-1909-coins-empathy), [[50]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#mor-stein-1917-einfuehlung-foreign-consciousness) |
| 1638–1894, physics | the string, the clock, the circuit | | [[51]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#res-galileo-1638-no-sympathy-word), [[13]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/physics#phys-huygens-1665-beam-cause), [[52]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-rayleigh-resonance-general-term) |
| 1990s– | the brain | | [[53]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neuro#emp-rizzolatti-1999-resonance-behaviors) ◐, [[54]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neuro#feel-gallese-goldman-1998-mirror-simulation) ◐, [[55]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neuro#emp-lamm-2011-pain-empathy-meta) ◐ |
| 2016– | society: a relation to the world | | [[56]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/social-theory#res-rosa-resonance-own-voice), [[14]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#soc-rosa-resonance-not-producible) |

## The turns, and what the texts do to each

**1. "It began as a cosmic bond."** It did not begin there. Problemata VII is titled "things arising from sympathy" and collects contagion between bodies: why we yawn when others yawn ([[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-problemata-vii-things-from-sympathy)). Brouwer argues, from the abstract we hold, that the word was first used for body and soul and that the Stoics extended it to the world [[31]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#anc-crit-brouwer-sympathy-began-body-soul) ◐. Even in the Stoic centuries Galen uses *sympatheia* for one organ suffering through another, and sets it against idiopathy [[33]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medical-ancient#anc-galen-frenzy-brain-by-sympathy-not-idiopathy). Cicero grants sympathy in the body and in nearby nature but refuses it for divination and fate [[57]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/stoic#anc-cicero-fato-contagio-granted-not-fate), [[58]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/stoic#anc-cicero-div-video-sympathian-dream-body). He has no single Latin word for it (*contagio*, *consensus*, *concentus*, *continuatio*) [[59]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/stoic#anc-cicero-latin-renderings-of-sympatheia). Ancient sympathy sat at three sites at once [[60]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/ancient#anc-arc-ancient-sympathy-not-only-cosmic).

**2. From cosmos to things.** The Neoplatonists kept the cosmic frame but changed its ground. For Plotinus, distant parts suffer together because the cosmos is one living animal [[34]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neoplatonic#anc-plotinus-iv4-32-sympathy-by-likeness-at-distance). Emilsson argues that this rests on an incorporeal soul and drops the Stoic physical medium [[61]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neoplatonic#anc-emilsson-plotinus-sympathy-incorporeal-not-stoic) ◐. That qualifies aliveness's edge [unverified]. Magic works through this sympathy ([[5]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-plotinus-magic-by-sympathy)). Proclus finds it in a single flower and stone: the heliotrope "prays" to the sun ([[15]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#fic-proclus-sacrifice-heliotrope-sings-to-sun-sympathy)), and the sunstone imitates the sun's rays ([[16]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-proclus-sunstone)). Iamblichus accepts sympathy among natures "as in one animal", but only as a lower cause of the rite ([[17]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/late-antique#lat-iamblichus-sacrifice-sympathy-subordinate)). Natural divination that works by "sympathetic necessity" is likewise far from the divine [[62]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neoplatonic#anc-iamblichus-divination-by-sympathy-lowly). This is the hinge on which the occult quality turns. Sympathy is now a property you can find in a particular stone, plant or animal, and the Renaissance catalogue follows from it: Agrippa's ladder ([[8]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/renaissance#ren-agrippa-sympathy-ladder)), Porta's chain ([[18]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-porta-sympathy)), and Fracastoro's "hidden agreement of things" [[39]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/natural-magic#em-fracastoro-sympathy-hidden-agreement).

**3. The controversy: occult quality to mechanism?** Partly, and not where the story puts it.
- The weapon-salve quarrel was not mainly about sympathy against mechanism. Both sides granted that the wound healed, and fought over whether the cause was natural or satanic [[40]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medicine#em-helmont-dispute-natural-or-satanic), [[19]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-libavius-god-demons-nature), [[20]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/natural-magic#nat-fludd-question).
- Mersenne attacked the world soul behind it, not sympathy as such [[63]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#em-mersenne-world-soul-does-not-exist).
- The mechanical turn began before the quarrel. Fracastoro had already called "occult property" a non-answer and explained contagion by tiny bodies in 1546 [[64]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medicine#em-fracastoro-against-occult-property), [[65]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/medicine#em-fracastoro-contagion-by-insensible-particles).
- Digby, the powder's champion, rejects "Sympathies" as a mere word [[66]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-digby-sympathy-a-word-not-a-reason) and explains the cure by atoms carried on light [[41]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-digby-atoms-carried-by-light). Kodera reads him as keeping the world soul as well [[67]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#em-crit-digby-translated-not-overcame) ◐.
- Descartes explains the "occult" effects by particles rather than denying them [[68]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-descartes-occult-effects-by-particles), and a Leipzig disputation still defends occult qualities in 1661 [[69]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-alberti-occult-quality-asylum).
- The real break is Boyle: sympathy and antipathy between lifeless bodies "depend upon the action of our own understanding" [[42]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#em-boyle-amity-enmity-only-in-minds).

So the occult quality was absorbed, not expelled [disputed]. The magnet carried sympathy through the century ([[21]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/philsci#phil-census-sympathy-magnet-17c)), and Huygens's clocks show the word becoming a placeholder for a cause not yet found ([[22]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/physics#phys-huygens-1665-sympathie-consonance), [[23]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/physics#phys-royal-society-pretended-sympathy)).

**4. From things to feelings.** This is the largest turn, and the texts make it a change of concept, not a migration of one concept [[70]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-new-concept-took-the-word) ◐.
- None of the moral writers grounds sympathy in cosmic *sympatheia*. Butler grounds it in affections God put in the heart, and in the fact that "men are so much one Body" [[43]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-butler-1726-so-much-one-body). Hutcheson grounds it in a "publick sense" [[71]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-hutcheson-1728-publick-sense).
- Hume makes it the communication of passions, an idea converted into an impression [[44]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1739-sympathy-communication), [[72]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1739-idea-becomes-passion).
- Smith makes it imaginative change of place [[45]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-changing-places-in-fancy), and himself notes the word's widening from pity to "any passion whatever" [[73]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-sympathy-any-passion).
- Rousseau puts *pitié* in the body, below reason [[46]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-rousseau-1755-pitie-precedes-reflection). Schopenhauer explains *Mitleid* by the unity of being, "tat tvam asi", which is the one return to a cosmic ground [[74]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-schopenhauer-1840-tat-tvam-asi).
- Nietzsche says the overvaluation of *Mitleid* is "something new" [[75]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#mor-crit-nietzsche-1887-overvaluation-is-new).
- Medicine kept the old bodily sense alongside the new one: Whytt's "sentient and sympathetic power" of the nerves ([[12]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-whytt-1765-sentient-sympathetic-power)).

**Does the string survive?** Unevenly [[76]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/historiography#feel-string-image-survives-unevenly).
- Hutcheson has "well-tuned Instruments" in 1728, as a picture of what people should be [[77]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-hutcheson-1728-well-tuned-instruments).
- Hume has "strings equally wound up" for passions passing between people [[78]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1740-strings-equally-wound), and he also uses mirrors [[79]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1739-minds-mirrors).
- Smith drops the string and keeps only concord: feelings "will never be unisons, they may be concords" [[80]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-no-string-image), [[81]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-unisons-concords).
- Lipps brings the string back, but inside one mind [[82]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/aesthetics#feel-lipps-1903-strings-in-me).
- In neuroscience the word "resonance" remains without the string [[83]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/historiography#emp-resonance-word-without-string) ◐.

**5. From feeling to a psychological capacity.**
- *Einfühlung* began as aesthetic projection into forms [[47]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/aesthetics#feel-vischer-1873-objective-einfuehlung). Source Library's English makes Vischer say "sympathy" where the German only means "affected" [[84]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/historiography#emp-vischer-1873-mitleidenschaft-not-sympathy).
- Lipps made it the way we know other minds [[48]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#emp-lipps-1903-einfuehlung-third-knowledge), and Jahoda reports that he took it to be like the old sympathy [[85]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/historiography#feel-jahoda-2005-shift-sympathy-empathy) ◐.
- Titchener's coinage is kinaesthetic: feeling pride "in the mind's muscles" [[49]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#feel-titchener-1909-coins-empathy). Vernon Lee calls empathy "analogous to moral sympathy" [[86]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/aesthetics#emp-lee-1912-empathy-analogous-sympathy), and Southard takes it into the clinic [[87]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#emp-southard-1918-empathic-index).
- The phenomenologists split what the word joined. Scheler separates fellow-feeling from contagion [[88]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-scheler-1913-four-forms), [[89]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#feel-crit-scheler-contagion-not-sympathy). Stein separates *Einfühlung* from *Einsfühlung* against Lipps [[90]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#mor-stein-1917-not-einsfuehlung).
- The modern literature counts 43 definitions [[91]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#emp-crit-cuff-2016-43-definitions) and eight phenomena [[92]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#emp-crit-batson-2009-eight-phenomena) ◐.
- The brain-level account is contested. Hickok argues against mirror neurons as the basis of understanding [[93]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#feel-crit-hickok-2009-eight-problems) ◐, and Cook et al. argue they are learned by association [[94]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#emp-crit-cook-2014-associative-mirror). Bloom and Prinz deny that empathy is a good moral guide [[95]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#feel-crit-bloom-2017-against-empathy) ◐, [[96]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#emp-crit-prinz-2011-against-empathy) ◐.

**6. Resonance, physical and social.** The mechanism came long before the word.
- Galileo explains the answering string by timed pushes, without using the word sympathy [[51]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/early-modern-science#res-galileo-1638-no-sympathy-word).
- "Sympathy" stays the name in Kircher in 1673 and Tyndall in 1867 [[97]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/natural-magic#res-kircher-1673-sympathetic-sounds), [[98]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-tyndall-sympathetic-vibrations). German says *Mitschwingen* [[99]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-helmholtz-mitschwingen-term).
- Rayleigh makes "resonance" the general term [[52]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-rayleigh-resonance-general-term), and by 1894 *Resonanz* names electrical circuits [[100]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-tesla-1894-electrical-resonanz) (synthesis: [[101]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/historiography#res-word-switch-synthesis) ◐).
- The social use did not wait for Rosa. Herder calls the human body a string instrument tuned to all beings [[102]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#res-herder-1785-human-string-instrument). Spencer makes vocal cadence the medium of sympathy ([[24]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#mus-spencer-1858-cadences-chief-media-of-sympathy)).
- Rosa keeps the violin but drops likeness [[56]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/social-theory#res-rosa-resonance-own-voice), [[103]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#res-crit-rosa-tuning-fork-likeness).

**The survivals break the line.** The old senses did not die when new ones arrived.
- Mesmer's fluid is read as cosmic sympathy made a physical medium ([[25]](/explore/histories/aliveness/claims/vitalism#vit-edge-animal-magnetism-descends-sympathy), partial).
- Townshend's mesmerism explains thought-transfer by "sympathetic vibration" in 1840 ([[26]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#soc-townshend-mesmeric-sympathetic-vibration)). Evans grounds mental healing in Proclus's "law of sympathy" in 1886 ([[27]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-evans-sympathy-proclus-magic)).
- Frazer names "sympathetic magic" in 1890 ([[28]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/anthropology#anth-frazer-sympathetic-earliest)), and Rozin finds its laws in modern minds ([[29]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/cognitive#cog-rozin-laws-modern-abundant), partial).

## *Ganying*: the history that does not fit the stages

The Han texts put omens, rulers' *qi*, music that moves Heaven, rain-making, the sick body before rain, and the answering zither under one rule of kind [[35]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-ganying-spans-levels).
- The body is inside the cosmos from the first text [[36]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-cfl-body-answers-weather).
- The moral sense is there from the start as well: fine deeds summon fine kinds [[104]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-cfl-fine-things-summon-fine-kinds).
- The Han authors disagreed about the mechanism. The Huainanzi calls it beyond knowing [[105]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-huainanzi-wulei-xiangying-beyond-knowing); the Chunqiu fanlu says "something makes it so" [[106]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-cfl-not-spontaneous-something-makes-it).
- Wang Chong accepts like moving like in nature but denies that punishments chill the weather [[107]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#ch-crit-wangchong-punishment-cold). Shen Kuo rejects the usual accounts of the ash-pipes ([[30]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/divination#w4mus-shenkuo-rejects-ganzhao)).
- The Song philosophers then make stimulus and response the pattern of all change, in which the response is usually the opposite of the stimulus [[38]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-zhuxi-ganying-pattern-of-all-change).

So the Chinese history runs from like answering like toward unlike answering unlike. That is the reverse of the European narrowing, and a reason not to translate 感應 as "sympathy" [disputed].

## Does the hypothesised arc hold?

| Stage | Holds? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1. cosmic bond | partly | Stoic, yes; but the body and divination were there from the start, and the word may have begun in the body |
| 2. occult quality | yes | through Neoplatonic "sympathy in the particular" to the Renaissance catalogue |
| 3. medical controversy | yes, reframed | the quarrel was natural against demonic, and mechanism absorbed the occult rather than defeating it; Boyle, not the weapon-salve, is the break |
| 4. moral feeling | yes, as a new concept under the old word | no moral writer grounds it in cosmic sympathy; the string image survives in Hutcheson and Hume, not in Smith |
| 5. psychological capacity | yes | but *Einfühlung* began as aesthetics, and "empathy" was kinaesthetic in 1909 |
| 6. physics and social theory | yes, separately | the physics word changed in the 1870s–90s, not the 1600s; the social use is older than Rosa (Herder, Spencer) |

**What the arc misses.** It misses survivals (mesmerism, New Thought, Frazer, homeopathic "like cures like"), the body as a constant site, and *ganying*.

**Share already on file.** This page cites 110 distinct claims. 31 of them (28%) were already on file in harmony, magic or aliveness, and 79 are new in this concept. Before this concept was built, harmony, magic, aliveness and soul held about 170 claims on sympathy, resonance, *ganying* or empathy. The periods that were already well covered were Stoic, Plotinus, weapon-salve, Huygens and Rosa. The new claims are mostly in the gaps: Galen and Cicero, the Han and Song *ganying* texts, the mechanical turn (Fracastoro, Descartes, Boyle), moral sympathy (Butler to Stein), and *Einfühlung* and empathy.

title: 2. Like and unlike: the line between resonance and harmony is drawn again in every sense of sympathy
md:
**Starting point.** Harmony's idea 12 argues that resonance is like answering like and harmony is unlike fitted together. Resonance is a mechanism of harmony, but resonance alone ends in unison and lock ([unverified], unverified proposal). That page works mainly with strings, clocks and *ganying* as acoustics. It notes that "sympathy sits between the two" and that Rosa's resonance "is not this one". This page does not restate it. It follows the distinction into the senses of sympathy that idea 12 does not treat: the Latin word, the moral feeling, empathy, Song-dynasty *ganying* and Rosa. It finds the same line drawn again in each.

**The claim of this page.** Each time sympathy moved to a new site, its writers split it into two things.
- One is like answering like: the self or the part merges with what it answers.
- The other keeps a difference and calls it concord.

The second is harmony's shape, in harmony's own terms. The cost idea 12 predicts for resonance alone (lock, unison, the loss of the unlike) reappears in each new site under a new name: contagion, *Einsfühlung*, personal distress, bias toward one's own kind.

## 1. The line is in the word from the first translation

Cicero renders *sympatheia* as "*coniunctio naturae et quasi concentus atque consensus*" [[7]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/stoic#anc-cicero-latin-renderings-of-sympatheia). *Concentus* is singing together, a harmony word, and *consensus* is feeling together. Latin gave sympathy a harmony word at its entry into Latin. The confusion idea 12 warns against ("say which sense is meant every time") is older than any modern author.

Plotinus keeps the two apart in the cosmos. Sympathy between distant parts works by likeness [[8]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neoplatonic#anc-plotinus-iv4-32-sympathy-by-likeness-at-distance), while "one harmony" is the order the sympathetic whole acts through ([[1]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/ancient#anc-plotinus-cosmos-one-harmony-sympathy)). Fracastoro's first sympathy is different again. It is a *consensus* by which all bodies cling together so that no vacuum opens [[9]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/natural-magic#em-fracastoro-first-consensus-no-vacuum). That is continuity, neither likeness nor harmony, a third option that idea 12 does not name.

## 2. Hume is resonance; Smith is harmony

The eighteenth-century moralists divide exactly on the line.
- **Hume** compares sympathy to "strings equally wound up", where the motion of one communicates itself to the rest [[10]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1740-strings-equally-wound). Equal tuning is the unison case: like answering like. The passion itself passes over, an idea "converted into an impression" [[11]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-hume-1739-idea-becomes-passion).
- **Smith** refuses the unison. Because the spectator only imagines the sufferer's situation, their feelings "will never be unisons, they may be concords" [[12]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-unisons-concords), and he never uses the string image [[13]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-no-string-image). Harmony already holds Smith's "keep perfect time" and "compleat harmony and concord" ([[2]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#soc-smith-1759-keep-perfect-time), [[3]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/social#soc-smith-1759-harmony-concord-sufferer)). What this concept adds is that he says *concord, not unison* in so many words. That settles idea 12's open placement of Smith ("sympathy sits between the two"): Smith's sympathy is on harmony's side, and he says so.
- **Hutcheson**, before both, asks people to be "like well-tuned Instruments, affected with every Stroke or Touch upon any one" [[14]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#mor-hutcheson-1728-well-tuned-instruments). It is resonance offered as an ideal of universal benevolence. Like Maier in idea 12, he promotes resonance to the whole of the good.

## 3. Empathy splits the same way, twice

**Phenomenology, 1913–1917.**
- Scheler separates emotional contagion, which "has nothing whatever to do with fellow-feeling", from fellow-feeling proper [[15]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#feel-crit-scheler-contagion-not-sympathy), [[16]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-scheler-1913-four-forms).
- Stein, against Lipps, says we do not know others by *Einsfühlung* (feeling-as-one) but by *Einfühlung*, in which the other stays other [[17]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#mor-stein-1917-not-einsfuehlung), [[18]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#mor-stein-1917-einfuehlung-foreign-consciousness).
- Contagion and *Einsfühlung* are like answering like, with the difference collapsed. Fellow-feeling and Stein's *Einfühlung* keep the unlike.
- Lipps, whom both attack, had built empathy on the sympathetic string *inside* one mind [[19]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/aesthetics#feel-lipps-1903-strings-in-me), and harmony holds his "Resonanz des Gleichartigen" ([[4]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/art#mus-lipps-1903-gesetz-resonanz-des-gleichartigen)). The phenomenologists' objection to Lipps is the objection idea 12 makes to resonance alone.

**Psychology and neuroscience, 1990s–2010s** (all from abstracts, so hedged).
- The modern definitions rebuild the same line. Decety and Jackson are reported to define empathy as felt similarity "without losing track of whose feelings are whose" [[20]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/neuro#emp-decety-jackson-2004-shared-representations) ◐.
- Singer and Klimecki reportedly let empathy "resonate with" others' feelings but call it emotional contagion when the self-other distinction is lost [[21]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#feel-singer-klimecki-2014-empathy-compassion) ◐.
- Hatfield's emotional contagion is the bare like-to-like case [[22]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/psychology#emp-hatfield-1994-emotional-contagion) ◐.
- Bloom's charge that empathy is "narrow" and "subject to bias" [[23]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#feel-crit-bloom-2017-against-empathy) ◐ reads, in idea 12's terms, as resonance's failure: it answers only what is like itself. Where Bloom prefers compassion, that is the other side of the line. This reading is ours, not Bloom's.

**What this means for harmony's thesis.** Idea 12 predicts that resonance alone ends in lock. In the psychology of empathy, "lock" has a name: contagion without a self-other distinction. The remedy the literature gives is harmony's remedy: enough difference kept, enough coupling to answer. This is an analogy between two literatures, not a finding of either.

## 4. *Ganying* crosses from like to unlike

Idea 12 cites *ganying* as like answering like, using the Han zither texts. The Han texts do say that: kinds summon kinds, strike *gong* and *gong* moves [[24]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-lushi-yingtong-lei-xiangzhao).
- The Song philosophers change the rule. For Zhu Xi, rain stimulates clear sky and clear sky rain, cold stimulates heat, and contraction stimulates expansion [[25]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-zhuxi-ganying-pattern-of-all-change), [[26]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/chinese#ch-chengyi-qushen-as-ganying). The response is usually the *opposite* of the stimulus.
- That is unlike answering unlike, the alternation of yin and yang, which is closer to harmony (*he*) than to *tong*. So "resonance" is the wrong English word for Song *ganying* [disputed] (the critique is ours; we found no published one).
- Even inside acoustics the line blurs. Zhu Zaiyu calls the *zhi* of Yize answering the *gong* of Dalü "like sounds answering" [[27]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#ch-zhuzaiyu-dalu-yize-tongsheng). If the two are different pipes a fifth apart, which is our reading and is hedged in the claim, the "like" is a concord. That is idea 12's shared-partials link stated in a Ming source.

## 5. Rosa takes the word and refuses its likeness

Idea 12 says Rosa's resonance "is not this one". The interview this concept adds shows Rosa saying so himself.
- Celikates and Lijster object that a body resonates only with what is of the same kind, the tuning-fork problem.
- Rosa answers that resonance needs an answering "own voice" and difference: "Resonance is not consonance" [[28]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#res-crit-rosa-tuning-fork-likeness).
- His model is a violin that resonates because it is "closed enough to have its own voice" [[29]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/social-theory#res-rosa-resonance-own-voice).
- In idea 12's terms, Rosa's resonance is harmony under resonance's name. The physicists had made the opposite move: Rayleigh restricts "resonance" to the case of nearly equal periods [[30]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/physics#res-rayleigh-resonance-general-term). Social theory took the word just as physics narrowed it to likeness. The verdict on the borrowing is in [[31]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#res-crit-verdict-borrowed-metaphor) ◐.
- New Thought made the opposite choice: "like attracts like" keeps only the resonance half of Philolaus ([[5]](/explore/histories/magic/claims/modern#mod-newthought-like-attracts-reverses-philolaus)). Between them, Rosa and New Thought mark the two ways the old word can be used today.

## What follows

- **For harmony's idea 12.** Place Smith on harmony's side, citing [[12]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/moral-philosophy#feel-smith-1759-unisons-concords). Treat Song *ganying* as alternation, not resonance. Add the empathy literature's contagion versus self-other distinction as a third domain where "resonance alone ends in lock" can be tested.
- **For writing.** Never translate *sympatheia*, *ganying*, *Einfühlung* or Rosa's *Resonanz* into "resonance" or "sympathy" without saying which side of the line the author is on. Several of them (Cicero, Rosa) put the word on one side and the meaning on the other.

## Open questions

- Is there an author who sees the line and rejects it, holding that understanding *requires* becoming like the other (Lipps's *Einsfühlung*, the mystics' union)? Stein names Lipps as one [[17]](/explore/histories/sympathy/claims/critique#mor-stein-1917-not-einsfuehlung). Is there a pre-modern one?
- Does antipathy have a moral and psychological afterlife (aversion, disgust, out-group bias), or did it stay in natural magic? The wolf and the sheep are well covered ([[6]](/explore/histories/harmony/claims/music#mus-kircher-wolf-polychord-test)); the later senses have no claims yet.
